espn-604007.headline: Ireland put a hooker at eight to meet the bomb squad
beats: Dan Sheehan, Ireland's captain and usual hooker, starts at number eight. That puts a front-rower in line to play the full 80 minutes, which almost never happens. His answer to South Africa's late replacements: "You have monsters that can go 80 minutes though."

South Africa arrive without Rassie Erasmus, banned for questioning the integrity of match officials. They lost 19–21 to France last time out, and they rarely lose two in a row. They also need this win to keep chasing New Zealand at the top of the southern table.
Ireland lost the same fixture on this ground last year, 13–24. They have since put 42 on Argentina and 43 on Fiji in Dublin this month, with 13 tries between the two.
If Ireland win and New Zealand and France win too, these two meet again at Twickenham on finals weekend. That leaves a week to think of something new.

espn-604008.headline: Lost to the Pumas, Italy pick a former Puma at 10
beats: Domingo Miotti, a 30-year-old former Argentina fly-half now at Montpellier, makes his Test debut for Italy in place of Paolo Garbisi. A week earlier, Italy lost 14–19 at home to Argentina.

Neither side has won in five rounds. Fiji conceded 54 and 43 to France and Ireland in a fortnight, and Italy let in 66 against South Africa. Captain Giacomo Nicotera's plan is control: lose it, he says, and Fiji will be comfortable.
The sides have met twelve times and won six apiece, the last in November 2017, when Italy won 19–10 in Catania. Win here and Italy go up to 10th, above Fiji.
Whatever happens, the two will probably meet again on finals weekend in the 11th-place final. Miotti's first Test may double as his rehearsal.

espn-604009.headline: The party was last week. France still have to turn up
beats: France beat South Africa 21–19 at the Stade de France on 13 November. Antoine Dupont is treating Argentina as a semi-final, with the door to the grand final on the other side.

Argentina come off a 42–12 beating by Ireland and a scrappy 19–14 win in Italy. They are without Juan Cruz Mallía, their best player, and the arrival of Shaun Edwards and Mario Ledesma on the staff has not yet steadied them.

France change plenty. Matthieu Jalibert is back at fly-half, Esteban Capilla makes his first start and François Cros is rested. Even a draw drops France to fourth in the world, below Ireland, a week after beating the Springboks.
Argentina have won twice in 2026. Dupont still cannot remember an easy game against them.

espn-604010.headline: Wales beat the All Blacks and still made four changes
beats: The 35–28 win last weekend was Wales's first over New Zealand in 73 years. Steve Tandy followed it by leaving out James Botham, player of the match after something in the region of 30 tackles. Adam Beard misses out with a shoulder injury.
Australia have lost four straight. New Zealand put 50 and 43 on them, England 45, and Scotland edged them 15–12. The last time these two met, in November 2024, Australia won 52–20.
Australia make five changes of their own. A Wales win by 16 or more would lift them above Australia into eighth in the world.
Finals day at Twickenham is next weekend. Wales would rather arrive with a habit than a single result to point at.
